author: EmuCore - Hub
title: RPCS3 clears stale PPU delay when starting a thread
summary: A PPU scheduling adjustment resets the sleep delay after a wait and checks the current function before applying the thread-start heuristic.
heroAlt: Montage comparing several PlayStation 3 console models.

blocks.text: A delay can outlive the wait that set it

RPCS3 uses host scheduling heuristics to pace emulated PPU threads. Pull request #19580 adjusts the sleep and start logic so a recorded hardware sleep delay is cleared after the CPU completes its sleep or wait path. Without that cleanup, a later scheduling decision can inherit timing state from an earlier wait, even though the thread has moved on.

The patch also narrows the delay heuristic: it avoids applying the special case when the CPU being evaluated is not the current PPU, and it checks the current function before relying on the expected value in general-purpose register 11 for `sys_ppu_thread_start`. Those checks keep a function-specific heuristic from acting on unrelated execution state.

This is a targeted correction to scheduler bookkeeping, not a new timing model. The thread-start path still uses the existing heuristic when its preconditions match; the new guards prevent that logic from crossing onto a different PPU or an unrelated function. Clearing the delay at the wait boundary makes the state transition explicit and easier to reason about during scheduling.

Thread timing can vary with host load, game behavior, and synchronization patterns. The patch makes the intended conditions more precise, but does not establish a universal performance or compatibility change by itself. Useful tests should cover thread start after sleep, calls from non-current PPU contexts, unrelated functions with similar register contents, and normal wait/resume sequences.
